questions.question: What is a benefit of smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle?

options.text: It serves no purpose.
It lets you use engine braking.
It is illegal.
You should not do it when other vehicles are near.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through downshifting is useful for riders. If you use engine braking, activate your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect you?

options.text: They make you sleepy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety can make you sleepy and reduce your ability to ride safely. Before riding, learn how any medication affects your body.

questions.question: What is a benefit of a shatter-resistant face shield?

options.text: It can protect your face during a crash.
It only protects you from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
You should not wear it with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect your face during a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: You may lose grip on one or both wheels.
You may stop sooner than expected.
You may get a flat tire.
It takes too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may lose grip on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: At least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.
Following distance does not matter.
Ride on the left side of the lane so drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep a four-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if road or weather conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should your motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms and legs completely.
Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever feels comfortable, regardless of safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For proper protection while riding, wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move to the shoulder to get out of the way.
Speed up to create distance between you.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only increase danger by encouraging faster tailgating.

questions.question: Which is NOT a goal of choosing the right lane position?

options.text: To help you avoid road hazards.
To help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
To help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
To help you be seen by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: To help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, and helps you avoid hazards. It should increase visibility, not reduce it.

questions.question: What is a use of a motorcycle horn?

options.text: It is useless.
Other people usually cannot hear it.
It can quickly get someone's attention.
It should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, motorcycle horns are quieter than car horns, so others may not always hear you. Never rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing you?

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop and wait for it to lose interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Ride toward it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride toward it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and ride toward it slowly. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of an accident?

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Do not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crashes, make sure others can see you. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and position your motorcycle correctly. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be operated in curves.
It should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle or motorcycle with a sidecar handles curves very differently from a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What do more than half of all motorcycle crashes involve?

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Riding at night.
Worn tires.
Riders with less than six months of riding experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of riding experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes involve riders who have less than six months of experience.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrow view so you can stay focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you, what does this mean?

options.text: They see you.
This will never happen.
They will not necessarily yield to you properly.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not necessarily yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but do not notice them.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
Blue with white lettering or symbols
White with black lettering or symbols
Red with white lettering or symbols

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what is usually best to do?

options.text: Relax on the handgrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip both handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, brake slowly on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of these is not protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, ankle-covering boots, and hearing protection even with a helmet.
